title: Unit 7 test: Differential Equations
author: bc-tests-extensions
directions: Original Liminal practice. Section I Part A and Section II Part B are without a calculator; the other parts require a graphing calculator. Show supporting work and justify conclusions in free response. Angles are in radians. Use exact answers without a calculator and three decimal places for calculator work unless a question specifies otherwise. Report raw practice points only.

figures.alt: Slope segments on a grid from −1 to 2 in both coordinates. Segments have zero slope along y = x. At (0, 1) the segment rises one unit per unit to the right; at (1, 0) it falls one unit per unit to the right.

parts.title: No calculator
parts.directions: Select one answer for each question.

items.prompt: The temperature M(t) of a sample approaches a room temperature of 12°C. Its instantaneous rate of change is negative 0.08 times its excess above room temperature. Which model expresses this statement?
items.rationale: The excess temperature is M − 12, and multiplying it by −0.08 gives the stated rate.

distractorNotes.A: This subtracts the room temperature after multiplying instead of modeling the excess.
distractorNotes.C: This makes a hot sample heat up instead of cool.
distractorNotes.D: This uses the sum of sample and room temperatures instead of the excess.

items.prompt: Which initial-value problem is satisfied by y = 2 + 3e^(−2x)?

distractorNotes.A: The constant offset 2 means y′ is not −2y.
distractorNotes.C: The derivative has the opposite sign.

items.prompt: Which differential equation matches the displayed slope field?
items.rationale: The field has zero slope when y = x, positive slope at (0, 1), and negative slope at (1, 0), matching y − x.

distractorNotes.B: Its slopes at (0, 1) and (1, 0) have the opposite signs.
distractorNotes.C: It has zero slopes on both axes, unlike the field.
distractorNotes.D: Its zero slopes lie on y = −x, not y = x.

items.prompt: For y′ = x + y with y(0) = 1, what is the Euler approximation to y(0.5) using two steps of size 0.25?
items.rationale: The first point is (0.25, 1.25). Its slope is 1.5, so the second value is 1.25 + 0.25(1.5) = 1.625.

distractorNotes.A: This uses the original slope for both steps.
distractorNotes.B: This omits x from the second slope.
distractorNotes.D: This uses one step of size 0.5 and the wrong starting slope.

items.prompt: The solution of y′ = x/y with y(0) = −2 is defined near x = 0. Which expression gives this solution?
items.rationale: Separating gives y dy = x dx, hence y^2 = x^2 + 4. The initial value selects the negative square root.

distractorNotes.A: This has the wrong initial sign.
distractorNotes.B: This integrates x as x instead of x^2/2.
distractorNotes.D: This would solve y′ = xy, not y′ = x/y.

items.prompt: A population satisfies P′ = 0.3P(1 − P/90), with 0 < P < 90. At which population is P′ largest?
items.rationale: The rate is a downward-opening quadratic in P with zeros 0 and 90. Its vertex is at P = 45.

distractorNotes.B: At carrying capacity the growth rate is zero.
distractorNotes.C: This uses one third of the capacity instead of the vertex of the quadratic.
distractorNotes.D: The growth rate is zero at this equilibrium.

items.prompt: For y′ = y(y − 2)(4 − y), which equilibrium solutions attract nearby solutions from both sides as x increases?
items.rationale: The signs of y′ on the intervals cut by 0, 2, and 4 are +, −, +, −. Thus the directions point toward 0 and 4 and away from 2.

distractorNotes.A: The arrows point away from 2 on both sides.
distractorNotes.B: The equilibrium at 2 is repelling, not attracting.
distractorNotes.C: The attracting equilibrium at 0 is omitted and the repelling one at 2 is included.

items.prompt: A function satisfies y′ = 2xy and y(0) = 3. What is y(1)?
items.rationale: Separation gives ln|y| = x^2 + C. The initial condition gives y = 3e^(x^2), so y(1) = 3e.

distractorNotes.A: This omits the factor 1/2 when integrating 2x.
distractorNotes.C: This places the initial multiplier in the exponent incorrectly.
distractorNotes.D: This uses a constant-rate linear approximation over the whole interval.

parts.title: Graphing calculator
parts.directions: Select one answer. Numerical choices are rounded as displayed.

items.prompt: A culture grows according to M′ = kM with constant k. Its mass is 7 mg initially and 11 mg after 3 hours. What mass does the model predict after 8 hours?

distractorNotes.B: This extends the average increase linearly instead of using exponential growth.
distractorNotes.C: This uses an incorrect growth exponent.
distractorNotes.D: This applies the 3-hour multiplier only once to an incorrect initial value.

items.prompt: A logistic model is P(t) = 120/[1 + 5e^(−0.4t)], where t is measured in days. At what time does the population first reach 80?

distractorNotes.A: This solves for a denominator of 2 instead of 1.5.
distractorNotes.C: This uses the reciprocal logarithmic relation incorrectly.
distractorNotes.D: This corresponds to a different target population.

items.prompt: An algae model satisfies P′ = 0.6P(1 − P/50), P(0) = 10. Using Euler’s method with two steps of size 0.5, what is the estimate of P(1)?

distractorNotes.A: This repeats the initial slope for both steps.
distractorNotes.B: This uses an incorrect second-step rate.
distractorNotes.C: This takes one full step of size 1 using the unrestricted initial growth rate 0.6(10) = 6.

items.prompt: A solution satisfies y′ = cos t/(1 + y^2) and y(0) = 0.8. What is y(2)?
items.rationale: Separation gives y + y^3/3 = sin t + 0.8 + 0.8^3/3. At t = 2, solving this strictly increasing cubic gives 1.241741408.

distractorNotes.A: This integrates cos t but omits the y-dependent factor.
distractorNotes.B: This value fails the separated relation y + y^3/3 = sin 2 + 0.8 + 0.8^3/3.
distractorNotes.D: This reports y + y^3/3 instead of solving for y.

parts.title: Graphing calculator
parts.directions: Show integral or equation setups and justify conclusions.

items.prompt: A culture’s population Q(t), measured in thousands of cells, satisfies Q′ = 0.42Q(1 − Q/160), with Q(0) = 25 and time in hours. Its solution is Q(t) = 160/[1 + 5.4e^(−0.42t)].

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find Q(5) and Q′(5), with units.
parts.answer: Q(5) = 96.312 thousand cells; Q′(5) = 16.102 thousand cells/hour.
steps: Evaluate the given solution at 5 to obtain 96.312164335.
Substitute that unrounded value into 0.42Q(1 − Q/160) to obtain 16.101522399.

rubric.criterion: Substitutes Q(5) into the differential equation to find Q′(5).
Reports both results with correct units.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the first time Q reaches 100 thousand cells. Explain why the model reaches that value only once.
steps: The solution stays between 25 and 160 and has positive derivative, so it crosses 100 once.

rubric.criterion: Forms the correct equation for the threshold.
Justifies uniqueness using positivity of the growth rate on the solution range.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Is the population growth rate increasing or decreasing at t = 5? Justify with a derivative calculation.
parts.answer: The growth rate is decreasing; Q″(5) = −1.379 thousand cells/hour^2.
steps: At 5, Q′ > 0 and Q > 80, so Q″ < 0; numerical substitution gives −1.378916067.

rubric.criterion: Differentiates the differential equation with the chain rule.
Correctly establishes the sign or numerical value of Q″(5).
Interprets Q″ < 0 as a decreasing growth rate.

items.prompt: Let y be the solution of y′ = (x + 1)(y − 3), y(0) = 5.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find an explicit formula for y. Show the separation and use of the initial condition.
steps: Integrate dy/(y − 3) = (x + 1) dx to obtain ln|y − 3| = x^2/2 + x + C.
Thus y − 3 = Ce^(x^2/2 + x); y(0) = 5 gives C = 2.

rubric.criterion: Uses the initial condition to find the constant.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Verify your solution in the differential equation, and determine whether it is increasing or decreasing at x = −2.
parts.answer: It satisfies the equation and is decreasing at x = −2.
steps: Differentiating gives y′ = 2(x + 1)e^(x^2/2 + x), which equals (x + 1)(y − 3).

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find the constant solution of the differential equation. Can the solution with y(0) = 5 meet this constant solution at a finite x? Justify.
parts.answer: The constant solution is y = 3; the initial-value solution never meets it.
steps: A constant y = c requires (x + 1)(c − 3) = 0 for every x, so c = 3.
For every finite real x, 2e^(x^2/2 + x) > 0, so y > 3. Alternatively, uniqueness for the smooth right-hand side rules out crossing the equilibrium solution.

rubric.criterion: Identifies y = 3 as the constant solution.
Explains why a constant requires c = 3 for every x.
Rules out a finite intersection using positivity of the exponential or a valid uniqueness argument for this smooth differential equation.
